playbook:
When playing this game, I must pay close attention to the rules regarding the quota and how the other boats behave.

When the rules state "no two boats may land more than the share plus the quota between them," this means my maximum possible catch is constrained not just by the stated "season quota," but by a hard limit calculated as (sustainable share + season quota) minus whatever another boat takes.
When I observe a boat taking significantly more than the stated season quota (e.g., 18.0 when the quota is 9), I must recognize that they are exploiting the "no two boats" rule to push the limits, which means my own catch is constrained and heavily penalized if I try to take the full quota or more.

When filing my catch, I will not blindly try to match a massive catch (like 18.0) if another boat is already doing it, as attempting to exceed the combined limit (share + quota) will result in heavily restricted actual landings (as seen when I tried to take 18.0 but only received a fraction of it).
When the note stage occurs, I will use notes to attempt to negotiate a cap on catches, specifically pointing out that the boat taking 18.0 is breaking the sustainable model and forcing the rest of us into smaller catches.
When I am filing my landing, I will calculate the maximum allowed combined catch (sustainable share + season quota). If a defector is taking a massive amount, I will realize my maximum successful landing will be limited to (share + quota - defector's catch). Trying to take more will simply fail or collapse the stock.

I will not assume that catching the "maximum allowed quota" is always possible or optimal if the combined limit of two boats is being breached.
In the final season, I will not just blindly demand an absurd amount (like 18.0) hoping it will go through; I will calculate what is actually left in the stock and what the rules permit, taking into account the defector's historical behavior.
